title: Continuum confinement in pure SU(3) gauge theory
open: Prove confinement in an appropriately defined continuum pure SU(3) theory—for example, a positive asymptotic string tension for large Wilson loops—and connect the statement rigorously to the physical spectrum.
status: Wilson’s lattice formulation dates to 1974. Strong-coupling expansions and numerical continuum extrapolations support confinement, but a general continuum proof is absent; a mass gap alone would not establish every confinement criterion.
why: Explains, rather than assumes, why isolated color charges do not occur.
key_works: Kenneth Wilson, 1974, *Confinement of Quarks*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445; Davoudi et al., 2022, *Report of the Snowmass 2021 Topical Group on Lattice Gauge Theory*, arXiv:2209.10758.

title: Analytic solution of the three-dimensional Ising critical point
open: Determine the critical theory’s scaling dimensions and operator-product coefficients analytically, or provide an exact constructive characterization from which they follow.
status: Open since the three-dimensional Ising model became a central statistical model. Conformal bootstrap methods give exceptionally precise numerical constraints, not an exact solution.
why: Provides a benchmark for interacting quantum field theories and universality.
key_works: El-Showk et al., 2012, *Solving the 3D Ising Model with the Conformal Bootstrap*, arXiv:1203.6064.

title: Four-dimensional scale invariance versus conformal invariance
open: Prove, or construct a counterexample to, scale invariance implying conformal invariance for unitary, local, relativistic four-dimensional quantum field theories under explicitly stated spectral and stress-tensor assumptions.
status: Versions have been studied for decades. Strong perturbative results and conditional arguments exist; the fully general nonperturbative statement depends delicately on hypotheses.
why: Determines whether scale-invariant phases can exist outside the conformal framework.
key_works: Yu Nakayama, 2015, *Scale Invariance vs Conformal Invariance*, arXiv:1302.0884.

title: Nonperturbative quantum gravity in de Sitter space
open: Define a nonperturbative quantum theory with positive cosmological constant and specify its observables, Hilbert-space interpretation, and semiclassical limit.
status: Proposed de Sitter holographic descriptions and lower-dimensional models exist, but no framework has achieved the completeness of well-understood anti-de Sitter examples.
why: Connects quantum gravity to a universe with accelerated expansion.
key_works: Andrew Strominger, 2001, *The dS/CFT Correspondence*, hep-th/0106113; Strominger, 2009, *Five Problems in Quantum Gravity*, arXiv:0906.1313.

title: Strong cosmic censorship at physically appropriate regularity
open: Establish generic inextendibility of maximal globally hyperbolic developments at a specified regularity, such as twice-differentiable metrics or finite-energy weak solutions.
status: Strong censorship is not one interchangeable conjecture: continuity-level formulations encounter counterexamples. Dafermos and Luk’s Kerr-interior work demonstrates why regularity thresholds matter.
why: Identifies the precise sense in which Einstein’s equations determine the future uniquely.
key_works: Dafermos and Luk, 2017/2025, *The Interior of Dynamical Vacuum Black Holes I: The C0-Stability of the Kerr Cauchy Horizon*, arXiv:1710.01722; DOI: 10.4007/annals.2025.202.2.1.

title: Stability islands and collapse in anti-de Sitter space
open: Characterize which small perturbations of anti-de Sitter spacetime remain globally regular, become quasiperiodic, or undergo turbulent transfer leading to collapse.
status: The 2011 weak-turbulence result motivated extensive numerical and analytic work. Stable islands exist, so “every small perturbation collapses” is not the correct target.
why: Explains gravitational thermalization and the limits of perturbative stability.
key_works: Bizoń and Rostworowski, 2011, *On Weakly Turbulent Instability of Anti-de Sitter Space*, arXiv:1104.3702.

title: Generic BKL behavior near cosmological singularities
open: Prove or delimit the conjectured local, oscillatory approach to generic spacelike singularities in four-dimensional general relativity.
status: Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz arguments date to 1970. Rigorous and numerical results cover important symmetry classes, but the generic inhomogeneous case remains incomplete.
why: Provides a predictive description of the classical approach to extreme curvature.
key_works: Belinski, Khalatnikov, and Lifshitz, 1970, *Oscillatory Approach to a Singular Point in the Relativistic Cosmology*; Hans Ringström, 2001, *The Bianchi IX Attractor*.

title: Gravity-mediated entanglement experiment
open: Demonstrate entanglement generated through a gravitational interaction while excluding electromagnetic, mechanical, and measurement-mediated alternatives to the claimed interaction channel.
status: Concrete proposals appeared in 2017. Preparing, isolating, and controlling sufficiently massive spatial superpositions remains the central experimental challenge.
why: Tests whether gravity can transmit a genuinely quantum resource.
key_works: Bose et al., 2017, *Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240401; Marletto and Vedral, 2017, *Gravitationally Induced Entanglement between Two Massive Particles Is Sufficient Evidence of Quantum Effects in Gravity*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.240402.

title: Consistent measurement of Newton’s gravitational constant
open: Reconcile independent measurements of Newton’s constant with mutually compatible uncertainty budgets, identifying hidden systematics rather than merely averaging discrepant values.
status: The measurement lineage begins with Cavendish. Modern methods still produce difficult-to-reconcile results; improvement is limited by systematic control rather than only statistical precision.
why: Resolves an unusually weak point in the measurement of fundamental constants.
key_works: Terry Quinn, 2014, *The Newtonian Constant of Gravitation—A Constant Too Difficult to Measure? An Introduction*; Li et al., 2018, *Measurements of the Gravitational Constant Using Two Independent Methods*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0431-5.

title: Time dependence of dark energy
open: Determine whether cosmic acceleration is consistent with a cosmological constant or requires evolving dark energy or modified gravitational dynamics.
status: DESI’s 2025 second-release analysis found dataset-dependent preferences for evolving dark energy, not a settled discovery; combinations and model assumptions materially affect significance.
why: Distinguishes fundamentally different explanations of cosmic acceleration.
key_works: DESI Collaboration, 2025, *DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints*, arXiv:2503.14738.

title: Primordial tensor-mode detection
open: Detect a primordial gravitational-wave contribution to cosmic microwave background polarization, separating it from lensing, Galactic foregrounds, and instrumental effects.
status: Experiments have established increasingly strong upper bounds; foreground-cleaned primordial tensor detection remains distinct from detecting ordinary gravitational waves.
why: Probes the energy scale and dynamics of the early universe.
key_works: BICEP/Keck Collaboration, 2021, *Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves Using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season*, arXiv:2110.00483.

title: Particle identification of dark matter
open: Detect a nongravitational interaction or other discriminating signature that identifies a dark-matter constituent and quantitatively connects it to the cosmic abundance.
status: Gravitational evidence is extensive; searches have excluded important model regions without establishing a universally accepted particle identification.
why: Determines what most gravitating matter is made of.
key_works: Boveia et al., 2022, *Snowmass 2021 Dark Matter Complementarity Report*, arXiv:2211.07027.

title: Axion abundance from strings and domain walls
open: Predict the post-inflationary QCD-axion abundance with controlled uncertainties across the enormous separation between defect-core and cosmological scales.
status: Numerical simulations have advanced substantially, but extrapolation of string dynamics and radiation spectra remains a major source of uncertainty.
why: Converts an axion cosmology into a reliable experimental mass target.
key_works: Gorghetto, Hardy, and Villadoro, 2018, *Axions from Strings: The Attractive Solution*, arXiv:1806.04677; Marsh, 2016, arXiv:1510.07633.

title: Higgs quartic self-coupling
open: Obtain a direct or sufficiently model-independent constraint on the four-Higgs interaction that tests its Standard Model value rather than merely allowing enormous deviations.
status: Triple-Higgs production is exceptionally rare. Studies of higher-energy colliders establish possible channels, not an achieved measurement.
why: Probes a part of the scalar potential inaccessible to the trilinear coupling alone.
key_works: Dong et al., 2025, *Probing Triple Higgs Production via the 4τ2b Decay Channel at a 100 TeV Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2504.04037.

title: First-generation Higgs Yukawa couplings
open: Measure or tightly constrain the electron and light-quark Higgs couplings individually, testing whether their masses arise from the Standard Model Higgs mechanism.
status: Higgs couplings to heavier particles are much more accessible. First-generation couplings remain especially difficult because of small rates and hadronic backgrounds.
why: Tests whether one mechanism gives mass to all charged elementary fermions.
key_works: Butler et al., 2023, *Report of the 2021 U.S. Community Study on the Future of Particle Physics*, arXiv:2301.06581.

title: Strong-CP problem
open: Explain why the physical QCD CP-violating parameter is extremely small while other interactions violate CP, and distinguish the explanation experimentally.
status: Formulated in the 1970s. Axions, special CP structures, and other constructions are viable research directions, not established solutions.
why: Could reveal new symmetries or particles.
key_works: Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440; R. D. Peccei, 2008, *The Strong CP Problem and Axions*, hep-ph/0607268.

title: Absolute neutrino mass scale
open: Measure the absolute neutrino mass scale through a kinematic observable, separating it from cosmology-dependent bounds.
status: KATRIN’s April 2025 result bounded the effective electron-antineutrino mass below 0.45 eV; this was a bound, not a positive mass measurement.
why: Completes a missing part of the particle mass spectrum and tests mass-generation models.
key_works: KATRIN Collaboration, 2025 results announcement and associated analysis.

title: Dirac or Majorana neutrinos
open: Establish whether neutrinos are their own antiparticles, through lepton-number violation or another discriminating observation.
status: The distinction has existed since the 1930s. Oscillations prove nonzero masses but do not distinguish Dirac from Majorana particles.
why: Reveals whether total lepton number is a fundamental symmetry.
key_works: Ettore Majorana, 1937, *Teoria Simmetrica dell’Elettrone e del Positrone*; Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay*, arXiv:1610.06548.

title: Direct detection of the cosmic neutrino background
open: Detect relic neutrinos from the early universe through a distinguishable capture or other interaction signature, rather than indirect cosmological effects.
status: The relic background is a standard cosmological prediction. Capture proposals face extremely small rates, endpoint backgrounds, and challenging energy resolution.
why: Observes an epoch earlier than the cosmic microwave background.
key_works: Steven Weinberg, 1962, *Universal Neutrino Degeneracy*; Cocco, Mangano, and Messina, 2007, *Probing Low Energy Neutrino Backgrounds with Neutrino Capture on Beta Decaying Nuclei*, hep-ph/0703075.

title: QCD critical endpoint
open: Establish whether the QCD phase diagram contains a critical endpoint at finite baryon density and, if so, locate it with controlled theoretical and experimental uncertainties.
status: Heavy-ion fluctuation measurements and lattice expansions constrain possibilities. Finite-density calculations and nonequilibrium effects prevent a definitive identification.
why: Reveals the phase structure of strongly interacting matter.
key_works: Mikhail Stephanov, 2009, *Non-Gaussian Fluctuations near the QCD Critical Point*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.032301.

title: Finite-density QCD sign problem
open: Develop a controlled computational method for physically relevant baryon densities whose cost remains useful as volume and precision increase, or establish limits for specified algorithm classes.
status: Reweighting, imaginary chemical potential, Taylor expansion, complex contours, and other methods work in restricted regimes; there is no general practical solution.
why: Unlocks first-principles dense-matter and phase-diagram predictions.
key_works: Troyer and Wiese, 2005, *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201; Davoudi et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.10758.

title: Unambiguous glueball identification
open: Identify hadronic resonances with quantitatively established predominantly gluonic structure, accounting for mixing with quark–antiquark and multihadron states.
status: Lattice calculations predict glueball spectra, and several experimental candidates exist. Mixing and overlapping resonances complicate definitive assignment.
why: Tests non-Abelian gauge-field self-interaction in its most direct bound-state form.
key_works: Morningstar and Peardon, 1999, *The Glueball Spectrum from an Anisotropic Lattice Study*, hep-lat/9901004; Crede and Meyer, 2009, *The Experimental Status of Glueballs*, arXiv:0812.0600.

title: QCD conformal-window boundary
open: Determine, for specified gauge groups and fermion representations, the flavor-number boundary between infrared conformality and confinement/chiral symmetry breaking.
status: Perturbation theory controls part of the high-flavor regime; lattice studies constrain individual theories but the boundary is not fully mapped.
why: Tests strongly coupled renormalization-group dynamics and composite-model possibilities.
key_works: Banks and Zaks, 1982, *On the Phase Structure of Vector-Like Gauge Theories with Massless Fermions*; Appelquist, Fleming, and Neil, 2008, *Lattice Study of the Conformal Window in QCD-Like Theories*.

title: Reliable neutrinoless-double-beta nuclear matrix elements
open: Calculate relevant decay matrix elements with quantified and cross-validated uncertainties, including many-body truncation, weak currents, and short-distance contributions.
status: Competing nuclear methods yield significant spreads. Better calculations are essential even if an experimental signal is discovered.
why: Converts a measured half-life into particle-physics information.
key_works: Engel and Menéndez, 2017, *Status and Future of Nuclear Matrix Elements for Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay: A Review*, arXiv:1610.06548.

title: Predictive low-energy fission fragment distributions
open: Predict fragment masses, charges, kinetic energies, and emitted neutrons for specified nuclei and incident energies, with controlled uncertainties rather than purely fitted distributions.
status: Energy-density-functional and time-dependent approaches reproduce important trends but do not yet offer uniformly reliable predictions.
why: Supports reactor modeling, waste characterization, and astrophysical reaction networks.
key_works: Schunck and Robledo, 2016, *Microscopic Theory of Nuclear Fission: A Review*, arXiv:1511.07503.

title: Stellar-energy carbon-12 alpha-capture rate
open: Determine the \(^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}\) rate at helium-burning energies with sufficiently small, defensible uncertainties.
status: Direct measurements at stellar energies are extremely difficult; extrapolation depends on interference and subthreshold nuclear states.
why: Sets the cosmic carbon-to-oxygen balance and influences later stellar evolution.
key_works: deBoer et al., 2017, *The \(^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}\) Reaction and Its Implications for Stellar Helium Burning*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.89.035007.

title: Cold dense-matter equation of state
open: Determine the pressure–density relation and composition of matter inside neutron stars, including whether phase transitions occur at accessible densities.
status: Mass, radius, tidal, and nuclear measurements constrain the relation but do not identify a unique equation of state.
why: Probes matter at densities unavailable in stable terrestrial samples.
key_works: Lattimer and Prakash, 2016, *The Equation of State of Hot, Dense Matter and Neutron Stars*, arXiv:1512.07820.

title: Hyperon puzzle
open: Explain how dense matter containing energetically favored hyperons can remain sufficiently stiff to support observed heavy neutron stars, or establish that hyperons are suppressed.
status: The tension has sharpened with massive pulsar measurements. Repulsive interactions and phase transitions offer candidate resolutions, not a uniquely established composition.
why: Connects strange nuclear interactions to compact-star structure.
key_works: Chatterjee and Vidaña, 2016, *Do Hyperons Exist in the Interior of Neutron Stars?*, arXiv:1510.06306.

title: Color superconductivity in nature
open: Establish whether quark matter in compact objects forms a color-superconducting phase and identify an observable signature that distinguishes it from competing compositions.
status: Pairing is theoretically compelling at asymptotically high density. The relevant phases at neutron-star densities and their observable consequences remain uncertain.
why: Would reveal an entirely new macroscopic quantum state of matter.
key_works: Alford, Rajagopal, Schäfer, and Schmitt, 2008, *Color Superconductivity in Dense Quark Matter*, arXiv:0709.4635.

title: Predictive core-collapse supernova explodability
open: Predict which stellar progenitors explode, their energies and remnants, from initial stellar structure without adjustable explosion prescriptions.
status: Multidimensional neutrino-radiation simulations produce successful explosions for many cases, but outcomes depend on progenitor structure, transport, turbulence, and microphysics.
why: Explains neutron-star and black-hole populations and chemical enrichment.
key_works: Woosley and Janka, 2005/2006, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae*, astro-ph/0601261; Boccioli and Roberti, 2024, *The Physics of Core-Collapse Supernovae: Explosion Mechanism and Explosive Nucleosynthesis*.

title: Fast-radio-burst emission mechanism
open: Identify the coherent radiation mechanism and emission location for fast radio bursts, explaining polarization, spectra, temporal structure, and environmental dependence.
status: Magnetars are linked to at least some bursts, but identifying a source class does not settle the coherent-emission physics or population diversity.
why: Explains one of the most extreme coherent electromagnetic phenomena known.
key_works: Bing Zhang, 2023, *The Physics of Fast Radio Bursts*, arXiv:2212.03972; DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.035005.

title: Coronal heating energy budget
open: Determine the relative contributions of reconnection, waves, and other processes to coronal heating across quiet regions, active regions, and open-field environments.
status: The puzzle dates to the identification of the hot corona. Realistic simulations reproduce important features, but a quantitatively closed, general energy budget remains absent.
why: Explains stellar atmospheres and improves space-weather modeling.
key_works: Gudiksen and Nordlund, 2005, *An Ab Initio Approach to the Solar Coronal Heating Problem*, astro-ph/0407266; Arregui, 2015, *Wave Heating of the Solar Atmosphere*.

title: Parker magnetostatic problem
open: Determine under which line-tied magnetic topologies smooth force-free equilibria exist, and when ideal evolution necessarily develops increasingly singular current structures.
status: Parker’s arguments motivated decades of work. Results depend on topology, boundary conditions, and the distinction between true singularities and thin current layers.
why: Establishes whether magnetic braiding naturally supplies coronal dissipation.
key_works: Eugene Parker, 1994, *Spontaneous Current Sheets in Magnetic Fields*; Pontin and Hornig, 2020, *The Parker Problem: Existence of Smooth Force-Free Fields and Coronal Heating*, DOI: 10.1007/s41116-020-00026-5.

title: Sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays
open: Identify the dominant accelerator populations and infer their composition, injection spectra, and maximum energies while accounting for magnetic deflection.
status: Anisotropy and composition measurements constrain candidates but do not provide a complete source census.
why: Identifies nature’s most powerful particle accelerators.
key_works: Hillas, 1984, *The Origin of Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays*; Alves Batista et al., 2019, *Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies*, arXiv:1903.06714.

title: Air-shower muon deficit
open: Explain why simulations underpredict muon-related observables in parts of the ultrahigh-energy air-shower data, distinguishing interaction-model deficiencies from composition or detector effects.
status: The discrepancy appears across multiple analyses; its magnitude depends on energy and observable.
why: Affects cosmic-ray composition inference and tests hadronic interactions beyond accelerator reach.
key_works: Albrecht et al., 2022, *The Muon Puzzle in Cosmic-Ray Induced Air Showers and Its Connection to the Large Hadron Collider*, arXiv:2105.06148.

title: Relativistic-jet composition and acceleration
open: Determine where jets convert magnetic energy into bulk motion and radiation, and establish their electron–positron versus baryonic content across source classes.
status: Imaging, polarization, spectra, and simulations constrain different regions but leave major degeneracies.
why: Explains how compact objects transport energy over enormous distances.
key_works: Blandford, Meier, and Readhead, 2019, *Relativistic Jets from Active Galactic Nuclei*, arXiv:1812.06025.

title: Quantum PCP conjecture
open: Determine whether approximating the ground-state energy of local quantum Hamiltonians within a constant fraction of the total interaction strength remains QMA-hard under the relevant formulation.
status: Open since the 2000s. The NLTS breakthrough and good quantum LDPC codes solve important neighboring problems, not the quantum PCP conjecture itself.
why: Establishes fundamental limits on approximating quantum matter.
key_works: Aharonov, Arad, and Vidick, 2013, *The Quantum PCP Conjecture*, arXiv:1309.7495; Natarajan and Nirkhe, 2024, *The Status of the Quantum PCP Conjecture (Games Version)*, arXiv:2403.13084.

title: Area law for general two-dimensional gapped ground states
open: Prove an entanglement area law for a suitably specified general class of two-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonians, or identify the necessary additional assumptions.
status: One-dimensional results are much stronger. Higher-dimensional generality remains a major obstacle despite many tractable models.
why: Determines when efficient tensor-network descriptions should exist.
key_works: Eisert, Cramer, and Plenio, 2010, *Area Laws for the Entanglement Entropy*, arXiv:0808.3773.

title: Three-dimensional self-correcting quantum memory
open: Construct a physically realistic three-dimensional local system whose quantum-memory lifetime grows favorably with system size at nonzero temperature, without continuous active correction.
status: Four-dimensional idealized models and constrained lower-dimensional constructions provide partial lessons; a practical three-dimensional solution remains unresolved.
why: Could radically reduce the overhead of quantum storage.
key_works: Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl, and Preskill, 2002, *Topological Quantum Memory*, quant-ph/0110143; Haah, 2011, *Local Stabilizer Codes in Three Dimensions without String Logical Operators*, arXiv:1101.1962.

title: Practical fault tolerance with quantum LDPC codes
open: Build an end-to-end architecture implementing useful logical computation with quantum LDPC codes under realistic connectivity, leakage, correlated noise, decoding latency, and hardware constraints.
status: Existence of asymptotically good codes is solved. Translating coding advantages into a robust physical machine is a separate engineering problem.
why: Could reduce physical-qubit overhead substantially.
key_works: Panteleev and Kalachev, 2022, *Asymptotically Good Quantum and Locally Testable Classical LDPC Codes*, arXiv:2111.03654; Bravyi et al., 2024, *High-Threshold and Low-Overhead Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory*, arXiv:2308.07915.

title: Exact quantum capacity of the depolarizing channel
open: Determine the quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel throughout the unresolved noise range, including whether improved degenerate codes close existing bounds.
status: Decades of upper and lower bounds leave a gap; single-letter coherent information is not generally the full answer.
why: Establishes a basic benchmark for quantum communication.
key_works: DiVincenzo, Shor, and Smolin, 1998, *Quantum-Channel Capacity of Very Noisy Channels*, quant-ph/9706061.

title: Nuclear-clock accuracy beyond first demonstrations
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Turn the thorium-229 nuclear transition into a clock with a complete uncertainty budget, reproducible long-term operation, and demonstrated advantages over leading electronic clocks.
status: Nuclear excitation and initial clock demonstrations are already milestones, not open targets. Controlling solid-state or trapped-ion shifts and readout remains unfinished.
why: Opens precision tests and potentially new clock architectures.
key_works: Peik et al., 2021, *Nuclear Clocks for Testing Fundamental Physics*; Zhang et al., 2024, *Frequency Ratio of the \(^{229m}\)Th Nuclear Isomeric Transition and the \(^{87}\)Sr Atomic Clock*.

title: Electron electric dipole moment
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Detect an electron electric dipole moment or exclude additional well-defined CP-violating model space using independent molecular or atomic systems.
status: Experiments have reached extraordinarily small upper limits without an accepted positive detection.
why: Probes new CP violation at scales beyond direct collider reach.
key_works: ACME Collaboration, 2018, *Improved Limit on the Electric Dipole Moment of the Electron*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-018-0599-8; Roussy et al., 2023, *An Improved Bound on the Electron’s Electric Dipole Moment*, DOI: 10.1126/science.adg4084.

title: Molecular parity-violating energy difference
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Measure the electroweak parity-violating energy difference between enantiomers with a signal that survives molecular-structure and instrumental checks.
status: Predicted for decades; the effect is extremely small and has motivated increasingly sophisticated spectroscopy.
why: Directly links the weak interaction to molecular handedness.
key_works: Martin Quack, 2002, *How Important Is Parity Violation for Molecular and Biomolecular Chirality?*; Quack, Stohner, and Willeke, 2008, *High-Resolution Spectroscopic Studies and Theory of Parity Violation in Chiral Molecules*.

title: Picogram matter-wave interferometry
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Demonstrate center-of-mass interference of a picogram-scale object with a verified spatially separated superposition; this is a proposed mass-scale milestone, not an existing record claim.
status: Molecular interferometry and levitated systems have advanced, but scaling requires simultaneous control of vibration, thermal emission, collisions, and preparation.
why: Tests quantum coherence in substantially more massive objects.
key_works: Fein et al., 2019, *Quantum Superposition of Molecules beyond 25 kDa*; Bassi et al., 2013, arXiv:1204.4325.

title: Atom-interferometric gravitational-wave observatory
subfield: Atomic, molecular, and precision measurement physics
open: Build an atom-interferometer observatory that achieves an astrophysically useful strain sensitivity in its intended frequency band under realistic laser, gravity-gradient, and environmental noise.
status: Long-baseline proposals and prototypes exist; full astrophysical sensitivity is an integrated-system target.
why: Opens gravitational-wave frequencies between existing detector classes.
key_works: Graham et al., 2013, *New Method for Gravitational Wave Detection with Atomic Sensors*, arXiv:1206.0818; MAGIS-100 Collaboration, 2021, *Matter-Wave Atomic Gradiometer Interferometric Sensor: MAGIS-100*, arXiv:2104.02835.

title: Superconducting phase of the two-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model
open: Establish the thermodynamic phase diagram and the existence, extent, and strength of d-wave superconductivity in physically relevant doped regimes.
status: Numerical methods strongly constrain competing stripe, magnetic, and pairing states, but finite-size, temperature, and method-dependent limitations persist.
why: Tests whether a minimal electronic model explains high-temperature pairing.
key_works: Qin et al., 2021, *The Hubbard Model: A Computational Perspective*, arXiv:2104.00064.

title: Microscopic origin of strange-metal transport
open: Explain linear-in-temperature resistivity and associated transport across specified strange metals while accounting for momentum relaxation and material-dependent scales.
status: Quantum-critical, hydrodynamic, and incoherent-metal approaches reproduce aspects. A universal “Planckian bound” should not be assumed without hypotheses.
why: Replaces quasiparticle-based transport where it fails.
key_works: Bruin et al., 2013, *Similarity of Scattering Rates in Metals Showing T-Linear Resistivity*; Hartnoll and Mackenzie, 2022, *Colloquium: Planckian Dissipation in Metals*, arXiv:2107.07802.

title: Superconducting order parameter of Sr2RuO4
open: Determine the order-parameter symmetry, spin structure, and nodal topology while reconciling thermodynamic, magnetic, strain, and time-reversal-sensitive measurements.
status: Discovered as a superconductor in 1994. The once-common simple chiral-p-wave assignment is not an adequate settled answer.
why: Resolves a benchmark unconventional superconductor and possible topological pairing platform.
key_works: Ramires and Sigrist, 2019, *Superconducting Order Parameter of Sr2RuO4: A Microscopic Perspective*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.100.104501.

title: Ground state of the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet
open: Determine whether the nearest-neighbor model has a gapped topological spin liquid, a gapless state, or another thermodynamic ground state, resolving numerical extrapolation disputes.
status: Decades of work have narrowed possibilities, but close competing states challenge methods.
why: Provides a canonical test of quantum frustration and fractionalization.
key_works: Yan, Huse, and White, 2011, *Spin-Liquid Ground State of the S=1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet*; Savary and Balents, 2017, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1601.03742.

title: Field-induced phase of α-RuCl3
open: Establish the nature of the field-induced state and whether claimed thermal signatures require a Kitaev-related chiral spin liquid.
status: Magnetic suppression and transport measurements reveal unusual behavior, but sample dependence and phonon contributions complicate interpretation.
why: Tests non-Abelian fractionalization in a real material.
key_works: Kitaev, 2006, *Anyons in an Exactly Solved Model and Beyond*, cond-mat/0506438; Broholm et al., 2020, *Quantum Spin Liquids*, arXiv:1905.07040.

title: Intrinsic spin-liquid response of herbertsmithite
open: Separate intrinsic kagome-layer excitations from disorder and interlayer defects, determining whether the clean material is gapped and topologically ordered.
status: Continuum scattering supports fractionalized interpretations, but defects make low-energy behavior difficult to assign uniquely.
why: Connects ideal frustrated models to experimentally realizable quantum matter.
key_works: Han et al., 2012, *Fractionalized Excitations in the Spin-Liquid State of a Kagome-Lattice Antiferromagnet*; Broholm et al., 2020, arXiv:1905.07040.

title: Unambiguous non-Abelian braiding of Majorana modes
open: Demonstrate noncommuting exchange operations with verified fusion and parity behavior, excluding ordinary Andreev-state explanations.
status: Zero-bias peaks and other candidate signatures are not by themselves proof of Majorana non-Abelian statistics.
why: Establishes the physical basis of a major topological-computing approach.
key_works: Alicea, 2012, *New Directions in the Pursuit of Majorana Fermions in Solid State Systems*, arXiv:1202.1293; Beenakker, 2013, *Search for Majorana Fermions in Superconductors*, arXiv:1112.1950.

title: Non-Abelian fractional Chern insulator
open: Realize and identify a non-Abelian fractional topological phase without a large external magnetic field, including convincing statistics or equivalent topological diagnostics.
status: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall phases are already established milestones. Non-Abelian order and operational braiding are stronger, separate targets.
why: Could make anyonic physics more tunable and device-compatible.
key_works: Bergholtz and Liu, 2013, *Topological Flat Band Models and Fractional Chern Insulators*, arXiv:1308.0343; Xu et al., 2025/2026, *Signatures of Unconventional Superconductivity near Reentrant and Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulators*, arXiv:2504.06972.

title: Continuity of deconfined quantum critical transitions
open: Determine which candidate Néel–valence-bond-solid transitions are genuinely continuous and which are weakly first-order, including the role of emergent symmetry.
status: Proposed in 2004. Large simulations reveal striking scaling alongside drifts that permit competing interpretations.
why: Tests critical phenomena beyond conventional order-parameter theory.
key_works: Senthil et al., 2004, *Deconfined Quantum Critical Points*, cond-mat/0311326; Nahum et al., 2015, *Emergent SO(5) Symmetry at the Néel to Valence-Bond-Solid Transition*.

title: Almeida–Thouless transition in three dimensions
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Determine whether a short-range three-dimensional Ising spin glass has an equilibrium spin-glass transition in a nonzero magnetic field.
status: Mean-field theory predicts an Almeida–Thouless line; finite-dimensional theory and simulations do not yield an uncontested settlement.
why: Distinguishes competing pictures of the organization of glassy states.
key_works: de Almeida and Thouless, 1978, *Stability of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Solution of a Spin Glass Model*; Young and Katzgraber, 2004, *Absence of an Almeida–Thouless Line in Three-Dimensional Spin Glasses*.

title: Thermodynamic stability of one-dimensional many-body localization
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Determine whether generic disordered interacting one-dimensional systems possess a stable many-body-localized phase at infinite time and size under clearly specified assumptions.
status: Finite-size experiments and simulations show localization-like behavior; rare thermal regions and long crossover scales complicate extrapolation.
why: Determines whether interacting matter can robustly evade thermalization.
key_works: Abanin et al., 2019, *Many-Body Localization, Thermalization, and Entanglement*, arXiv:1804.11065; Sierant et al., 2025, *Many-Body Localization: Current Status and Open Questions*.

title: Higher-dimensional localization and thermal avalanches
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Establish whether stable many-body localization can exist in two or more dimensions for specified local models, or prove that thermal avalanches inevitably destroy it.
status: Avalanche arguments challenge stability; finite experimental and numerical systems cannot directly settle asymptotic behavior.
why: Defines the dimensional limits of nonthermal quantum phases.
key_works: De Roeck and Huveneers, 2017, *Stability and Instability towards Delocalization in Many-Body Localization Systems*; Abanin et al., 2019, arXiv:1804.11065.

title: Fourier’s law from deterministic microscopic dynamics
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Prove normal heat conduction with finite conductivity for a sufficiently broad, physically realistic class of deterministic interacting systems.
status: Exact and rigorous results exist for selected stochastic or special models. Generic deterministic systems remain difficult, especially in low dimensions.
why: Derives a basic macroscopic transport law from microscopic mechanics.
key_works: Bonetto, Lebowitz, and Rey-Bellet, 2000, *Fourier’s Law: A Challenge to Theorists*, math-ph/0002052.

title: Exact structure of 2+1-dimensional KPZ universality
subfield: Statistical mechanics and nonequilibrium quantum matter
open: Determine exact critical exponents, distributions, or an equivalent solvable characterization of the strong-coupling Kardar–Parisi–Zhang universality class in two spatial dimensions.
status: One-dimensional KPZ is far more analytically developed. Higher-dimensional exponents are primarily numerical.
why: Explains broad classes of nonequilibrium growth and fluctuating interfaces.
key_works: Kardar, Parisi, and Zhang, 1986, *Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889; Halpin-Healy and Takeuchi, 2015, *A KPZ Cocktail—Shaken, Not Stirred…*, arXiv:1505.01910.

title: Gardner phase in finite-dimensional structural glasses
subfield: Soft matter, granular matter, and active materials
open: Determine whether a sharp Gardner transition survives in realistic finite-dimensional glasses or becomes an avoided transition or crossover.
status: Mean-field theory predicts hierarchical marginal states; simulations and experiments give suggestive but interpretation-dependent signatures.
why: Links glass stability, marginality, and mechanical response.
key_works: Charbonneau et al., 2014, *Fractal Free Energy Landscapes in Structural Glasses*; Berthier et al., 2019, *Gardner Physics in Amorphous Solids and Beyond*.

title: Three-dimensional Navier–Stokes regularity
open: Prove global smoothness or construct finite-time breakdown for the incompressible three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations under the Clay problem’s conditions.
status: Global weak solutions have been known since Leray; smoothness and uniqueness in the required generality remain open.
why: Resolves a foundational question about deterministic fluid evolution.
key_works: Jean Leray, 1934, *Sur le Mouvement d’un Liquide Visqueux Emplissant l’Espace*; Charles Fefferman, 2000, *Existence and Smoothness of the Navier–Stokes Equation*.
prize: US$1 million Clay Millennium Prize, subject to its rules.

title: Turbulent intermittency exponents
open: Derive anomalous scaling exponents and extreme-event statistics of three-dimensional turbulence from the governing equations rather than empirical multifractal fits.
status: Kolmogorov’s 1941 theory gives a baseline; intermittency corrections remain incompletely understood.
why: Predicts rare, intense events important for mixing, loads, and reaction rates.
key_works: Uriel Frisch, 1995, *Turbulence: The Legacy of A. N. Kolmogorov*, DOI: 10.1017/CBO9781139170666.

title: Net-positive large-scale active drag reduction
open: Demonstrate sustained drag reduction whose saved power substantially exceeds actuation, sensing, and control costs under realistic fouling and changing flow conditions.
status: Large drag reductions occur in selected laboratory conditions; net energy benefit and robustness often diminish during scale-up.
why: Reduces transportation and pumping energy.
key_works: Quadrio, 2011, *Drag Reduction in Turbulent Boundary Layers by In-Plane Wall Motion*; Choi, Jeon, and Kim, 2008, *Control of Flow over a Bluff Body*.

title: Disruption avoidance at reactor conditions
open: Predict and avoid damaging plasma disruptions across operating scenarios with sufficiently low missed-event and false-alarm rates, and validated fallback mitigation.
status: Machine-learning predictors and mitigation experiments improve performance but must generalize across machines and operating regimes.
why: Protects reactor structures and supports high availability.
key_works: Hender et al., 2007, *Chapter 3: MHD Stability, Operational Limits and Disruptions*; de Vries et al., 2011, *Survey of Disruption Causes at JET*.

title: Vacuum Schwinger pair production
open: Observe electron–positron creation from the vacuum by an applied electromagnetic field in a regime that cleanly identifies the nonperturbative Schwinger mechanism.
status: Predicted in 1951. Strong-field pair production through other mechanisms is not the same observation.
why: Tests a central nonperturbative prediction of quantum electrodynamics.
key_works: Julian Schwinger, 1951, *On Gauge Invariance and Vacuum Polarization*; Di Piazza et al., 2012, *Extremely High-Intensity Laser Interactions with Fundamental Quantum Systems*, arXiv:1111.3886.

title: Laboratory optical vacuum birefringence
open: Measure the polarization-dependent refractive response of the quantum vacuum to a controlled applied field, excluding material and instrumental birefringence.
status: Strong theoretical prediction and astrophysical indications do not replace a clean laboratory optical measurement.
why: Directly tests nonlinear vacuum electrodynamics.
key_works: Heisenberg and Euler, 1936, *Folgerungen aus der Diracschen Theorie des Positrons*; Di Piazza et al., 2012, arXiv:1111.3886.

title: Solid metallic hydrogen and its retained phases
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: Establish the structures, electronic properties, and reproducibility of metallic solid hydrogen, including whether any useful phase can persist after pressure reduction.
status: Conducting dense hydrogen and debated solid-state claims do not settle the complete structural and metastability questions.
why: Tests extreme quantum matter and potential high-energy-density materials.
key_works: Wigner and Huntington, 1935, *On the Possibility of a Metallic Modification of Hydrogen*; McMahon et al., 2012, *The Properties of Hydrogen and Helium under Extreme Conditions*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.84.1607.

title: Predictive thermal boundary conductance
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: Calculate interface heat conductance from atomic structure, bonding, disorder, and temperature with accuracy transferable across dissimilar materials.
status: Acoustic and diffuse-mismatch models capture limits; real interfaces require anharmonic, electronic, and structural effects.
why: Removes a major bottleneck in electronics and thermal-management design.
key_works: Swartz and Pohl, 1989, *Thermal Boundary Resistance*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.61.605; Chen et al., 2022, *Interfacial Thermal Resistance: Past, Present, and Future*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.94.025002.

title: Microscopic identity of amorphous two-level systems
subfield: Chemical physics, thermal physics, and extreme materials
open: Identify the atomic structures and dynamics responsible for low-temperature two-level-system behavior in relevant amorphous materials and predict their density and coupling.
status: Phenomenological tunneling models date to the 1970s; a universal microscopic account remains elusive.
why: Reduces loss and noise in superconducting circuits, resonators, and precision sensors.
key_works: Anderson, Halperin, and Varma, 1972, *Anomalous Low-Temperature Thermal Properties of Glasses and Spin Glasses*; Phillips, 1972, *Tunneling States in Amorphous Solids*.

title: Functional significance of neural criticality
open: Determine whether observed scale-free neural activity reflects genuine critical dynamics and whether proximity to criticality causally improves computation or behavior.
status: Avalanche statistics motivate criticality models, but subsampling, nonstationarity, and alternative mechanisms can generate similar signatures.
why: Tests a proposed organizing principle of brain dynamics.
key_works: Beggs and Plenz, 2003, *Neuronal Avalanches in Neocortical Circuits*; Wilting and Priesemann, 2019, *25 Years of Criticality in Neuroscience—Established Results, Open Controversies, Novel Concepts*.

title: Lightning initiation
open: Explain how measured thundercloud conditions initiate leaders and breakdown, resolving the gap between observed large-scale fields and simple conventional-breakdown thresholds.
status: Streamer, hydrometeor-enhancement, and runaway-electron mechanisms provide candidate ingredients; their respective roles remain debated.
why: Explains a basic atmospheric electrical process and improves protection models.
key_works: Dwyer and Uman, 2014, *The Physics of Lightning*, DOI: 10.1016/j.physrep.2013.09.004.

title: Collider-grade muon cooling
open: Demonstrate the integrated six-dimensional phase-space cooling, transmission, and timing needed for a useful high-energy muon collider before excessive muon decay.
status: Ionization cooling is experimentally demonstrated; collider-grade integrated performance is a much stronger requirement.
why: Could enable compact access to very high lepton-collision energies.
key_works: MICE Collaboration, 2020, *Demonstration of Cooling by the Muon Ionization Cooling Experiment*; International Muon Collider Collaboration, 2024, *Interim Report*, arXiv:2407.12450.

title: Low-loss gravitational-wave mirror coatings
open: Produce optical coatings combining low mechanical loss, low absorption, high reflectivity, low scatter, and manufacturability at the intended temperature and wavelength.
status: Improving one property often degrades another; coating thermal noise limits important detector bands.
why: Increases gravitational-wave observatory sensitivity without simply increasing laser power.
key_works: Harry et al., 2002, *Thermal Noise in Interferometric Gravitational Wave Detectors Due to Dielectric Optical Coatings*; Granata et al., 2020, *Amorphous Optical Coatings of Present Gravitational-Wave Interferometers*.

title: Newtonian-noise cancellation for ground-based observatories
open: Predict and subtract gravity fluctuations from moving ground and air well enough to reach intended low-frequency sensitivity without subtracting genuine signals.
status: Sensor-array methods and site models provide partial demonstrations; realistic environmental variability complicates full cancellation.
why: Opens lower-frequency gravitational-wave observations from Earth.
key_works: Jan Harms, 2015, *Terrestrial Gravity Fluctuations*, arXiv:1507.05850.

title: Cosmic coincidence problem
open: the energy densities of dark energy and dark matter are of the same order of magnitude in the Universe. Dark matter energy density decreased during the evolution of the universe, so it must have been very large in the past. Is there any relation between the two energy densities?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Cosmological constant problem
open: Why does the [[zero-point energy]] of the [[vacuum]] not cause a large [[cosmological constant]]? What cancels it out?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Shape of the universe
open: What is the 3-[[manifold]] of [[comoving coordinates|comoving space]], i.e., of a comoving spatial section of the universe, informally called the "shape" of the universe? Neither the curvature nor the topology is presently known, though the curvature is known to be "close" to zero on observable scales. Is the shape unmeasurable; the Poincaré space; or another 3-manifold?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Magnetic monopole
open: s: Did particles that carry "magnetic charge" exist in some past, higher-energy epoch? If so, do any remain today? ([[Paul Dirac]] showed the existence of some types of magnetic monopoles would explain [[charge quantization]].){{cite journal

title: Neutron lifetime puzzle
open: While the neutron lifetime has been studied for decades, there currently exists a lack of [[consilience]] on its exact value, due to different results from two experimental methods ("bottle" versus "beam")
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Generations of matter
open: Why are there three generations of [[quark]]s and [[lepton]]s? Is there a theory that can explain the masses of particular quarks and leptons in particular generations from first principles (a theory of [[Yukawa coupling]]s)?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Neutrino mass
open: What is the absolute mass of neutrinos? Are they [[Dirac fermion|Dirac]] or [[Majorana fermion|Majorana]] fermions? Is the [[Neutrino mass hierarchy|mass hierarchy]] normal or inverted? Is the CP violating phase equal to 0?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Anomalous magnetic dipole moment
open: Why is the experimentally measured value of the [[muon]]'s anomalous magnetic dipole moment ("muon  − 2}}") significantly different from the theoretically predicted value of that physical constant? − 2}}) theory value: Present and future |class=hep-ph |eprint=1311.2198 }}
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Koide formula
open: An aspect of the [[Generation (particle physics)|problem of particle generations]]. The sum of the masses of the three charged [[lepton]]s, divided by the square of the sum of the roots of these masses, to within one standard deviation of observations, is  }}. It is unknown how such a simple value comes about, and why it is the exact arithmetic average of the possible extreme values of  (equal masses) and 1 (one mass dominates)
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Kuiper cliff
open: Why does the number of objects in the Solar System's [[Kuiper belt]] fall off rapidly and unexpectedly beyond a radius of 50 astronomical units?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Flyby anomaly
open: Why is the observed energy of satellites [[Gravity assist|flying by planetary bodies]] sometimes different by a minute amount from the value predicted by theory?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: The lithium problem
open: Why is there a discrepancy between the amount of lithium-7 predicted to be produced in [[Big Bang nucleosynthesis]] and the amount observed in very old stars?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Gauge block wringing
open: What mechanism allows gauge blocks to be wrung together?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

open: s: Can the [[nematic]] to [[smectic]] (A) phase transition in liquid crystal states be characterized as a [[Background independence|universal]] phase transition?A. A. Ramamoorthy, Springer 2007, chapter 8
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Metal whiskering
open: In electrical devices, some metallic surfaces may spontaneously grow fine metallic whiskers, which can lead to equipment failures. While compressive mechanical stress is known to encourage whisker formation, the growth mechanism has yet to be determined
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: The injection problem
open: [[Fermi acceleration]] is thought to be the primary mechanism that accelerates astrophysical particles to high energy. However, it is unclear what mechanism causes those particles to initially have energies high enough for Fermi acceleration to work on them
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Langmuir's paradox
open: In low-pressure plasmas, observed electron velocity distributions are often [[Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution|Maxwellian]] despite electron–electron collisions being too infrequent for [[thermalization]]
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Neutron drip-line map
open: Determine the last bound neutron-rich isotopes across the nuclear chart and explain their positions using predictive continuum-coupled many-body theory.
status: Light-element boundaries are much better mapped than heavy ones. Extrapolation becomes difficult near weak binding and changing shell structure.
why: Defines the limits of nuclear existence and constrains nucleosynthesis.
key_works: Erler et al., 2012, *The Limits of the Nuclear Landscape*, DOI: 10.1038/nature11188.

title: Nonlinear fate of extremal Kerr perturbations
open: Determine the nonlinear endpoint of physically admissible perturbations of exactly extremal rotating black holes, including whether horizon instabilities destroy extremality or generate new singular behavior.
status: Linear horizon instabilities have been studied since Aretakis’s work. Hintz’s June 2026 preprint claims full **subextremal** Kerr stability; that does not settle the extremal problem.
why: Resolves a boundary case where ordinary black-hole stability arguments change qualitatively.
key_works: Stefanos Aretakis, 2011, *Stability and Instability of Extreme Reissner–Nordström Black Hole Spacetimes for Linear Scalar Perturbations I*; Peter Hintz, 2026, *Nonlinear Stability of Subextremal Kerr Black Holes*, arXiv:2606.28253.

title: Hawking radiation from an astrophysical black hole
open: Detect radiation attributable to the Hawking process from an actual gravitational black hole, with competing emission mechanisms excluded.
status: Predicted in 1974–1975. Analogue-horizon experiments are valuable but do not constitute detection from an astrophysical black hole.
why: Directly tests the meeting point of quantum fields, curved spacetime, and thermodynamics.
key_works: Stephen Hawking, 1975, *Particle Creation by Black Holes*, DOI: 10.1007/BF02345020; Mann, 2026, *Black-hole Thermodynamics*.

title: QCD axion discovery
open: Detect an axion with mass and couplings consistent with solving the strong-CP problem, distinguishing it from a generic axion-like particle.
status: Proposed in the 1970s. Haloscopes, helioscopes, and laboratory searches cover complementary but incomplete parameter regions.
why: Could simultaneously explain dark matter and the suppression of strong CP violation.
key_works: Peccei and Quinn, 1977, *CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles*; David Marsh, 2016, *Axion Cosmology*, arXiv:1510.07633.

title: Neutrino mass ordering
open: Determine whether the third neutrino mass eigenstate lies above or below the closely spaced solar pair, with robust treatment of oscillation and detector uncertainties.
status: Global fits provide preferences rather than a universally decisive measurement. JUNO’s first published 2026 oscillation results improved solar-parameter measurements; they did not themselves settle ordering.
why: Changes the interpretation of neutrinoless double-beta decay and flavor models.
key_works: JUNO Collaboration, 2026 first reactor-oscillation results, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10538-z.

title: Atmospheric mixing-angle octant
open: Determine whether the atmospheric mixing angle is below, above, or exactly at maximal mixing, resolving degeneracies with other oscillation parameters.
status: Precision has improved substantially since atmospheric oscillations were established. Octant determination remains distinct from proving oscillations or measuring a mass splitting.
why: Discriminates flavor-symmetry models.
key_works: de Gouvêa et al., 2022, arXiv:2209.07983.

title: Net-electric fusion power
open: Operate a fusion system that exports sustained net electricity after accounting for drivers, magnets, cryogenics, fuel processing, cooling, and maintenance.
status: Plasma gain and target gain are not net-electric gain. Integrated electricity production remains a stronger engineering target.
why: Establishes fusion as an energy technology rather than only a plasma milestone.
key_works: National Academies, 2021, *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991.

title: Reproducible ambient-pressure room-temperature superconductivity
open: Produce a material superconducting near ordinary room temperature at ambient pressure, independently replicated through resistance, magnetic, and thermodynamic evidence.
status: High-pressure hydrides demonstrate very high transition temperatures. Controversial ambient-pressure claims do not satisfy the required evidence standard.
why: Could transform electrical systems, magnets, and sensing, subject to current-density and manufacturability constraints.
key_works: Drozdov et al., 2019, *Superconductivity at 250 K in Lanthanum Hydride under High Pressures*, arXiv:1812.01567; Pickett, 2023, *Colloquium: Room Temperature Superconductivity: The Roles of Theory and Materials Design at High Pressure*.

title: Yang–Mills theory
open: Given an arbitrary [[compact space|compact]] [[gauge symmetry|gauge group]], does a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory with a finite [[mass gap]] exist? (This problem is also listed as one of the [[Millennium Prize Problems]] in mathematics.)
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Quantum field theory
open: (this is a generalization of the previous problem): Is it possible to construct, in a mathematically rigorous way, a quantum field theory in 4-dimensional spacetime that includes interactions and does not resort to [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbative methods]]?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Dark matter
open: What is the identity of dark matter? Is it a [[Elementary particle|particle]]? If so, is it a [[weakly interacting massive particles|WIMP]], [[axion]], the lightest [[superpartner]] (LSP), or some other particle? Or, are the [[Galaxy rotation curve|phenomena attributed to dark matter]] the result of [[Modified models of gravity|an alternate theory of gravity]] separate from [[general relativity]] altogether? Despite extensive research, the exact composition of dark matter remains unknown. It is inferred from gravitational effects on visible matter, radiation, and the universe's large-scale structure. Understanding its properties is crucial for a comprehensive understanding of the universe
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Galaxy rotation problem
open: Is [[dark matter]] responsible for differences in observed and theoretical speed of stars revolving around the centre of galaxies, or is it something else? [[File:GalacticRotation2.svg|frame|right|Rotation curve of a typical spiral galaxy: predicted (A) and observed (B). Can the discrepancy between the curves be attributed to dark matter?]]
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics

title: Topological order
open: Is topological order stable at non-zero [[temperature]]? Equivalently, is it possible to have three-dimensional [[Stabilizer code|self-correcting]] [[Qubit|quantum memory]]?
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20physics
